newsitem.title: USA: Woman tells of bugs at Michael Jackson's ranch.
newsitem.headline: Woman tells of bugs at Michael Jackson's ranch.

text.p: One of five former employees who sued pop star Michael Jackson for wrongful termination testified Wednesday that she had been told to eavesdrop on staff at Jackson's Neverland ranch.

Sandi Domz, who was an administrative assistant at the ranch, told the court she saw listening devices at the sprawling complex in the mountains near Santa Barbara and was told information she gleaned would be passed on to Jackson.
"They wanted to hear what the employees were saying," she said under questioning from her attorney Michael Ring.

Domz, along with three of Jackson's former bodyguards and a maid have sued Jackson and six of his aides, alleging they installed recording devices to find out what they knew about molestation allegations against the self-styled "King of Pop."
The plaintiffs say they were forced out of their jobs. Jackson denies the allegations.

In 1993 a 13-year-old boy said Jackson molested him. The boy sued Jackson but the lawsuit was settled out of court for a reported $15 million. Jackson, who has denied any wrongdoing, was never charged with a crime.

Before a two-man, 10-woman jury in Santa Barbara County Court in Santa Maria, 125 miles (200 km) north of Los Angeles, Domz told how she was told to listen in on phone conversations of security staff.
She said she told Bill Bray, the head of security at Neverland, and Marcus Johnson, another security expert, about conversations she heard.
Johnson later showed her a transmitter on a window ledge of another woman's office that led to a receiver in her own office, Domz said.
She was able to pick up the woman's conversations, she said. Other listening devices were lcoated in other parts of the main building at Neverland, she said.
